findings.explanation: network_interface, image, kms_key_id, and resource_policies in this same file all use precise types (object({...}), a non-empty string with validation) — but tags (line 49) and service_scope (line 76) are still list(any), so Terraform can't catch a non-string element (e.g. a number or map slipped into the list) until it hits the provider at apply time. No deterministic rule catches this: HLD_TF_012 only checks that *a* type is declared, not how loosely, so a bare list(any) already satisfies it.
findings.remediation: Change both to list(string) — every current usage (tags applied to the instance/firewall target_tags, OAuth scope URLs) is already a plain string.
findings.title: tags and service_scope remain list(any) while sibling variables in the same file were tightened to strict types

findings.explanation: The root module tightened these exact two inputs to object({...}) types earlier in this session (variables.tf:12-16, 58-61) specifically so Terraform catches a missing/misspelled key at plan time instead of a runtime index error. example/examplea/variables.tf:12 and :31 still declare them as map(any), so the type safety gained at the module boundary is invisible one hop up — a typo in examplea.auto.tfvars would still only surface as a conversion error deep in module.bastion's evaluation rather than at this file's own validation. Terraform's structural typing means it still works today (confirmed via terraform validate), so this is a documentation/consistency gap, not a functional break.
findings.remediation: Mirror the module's types exactly: network_interface as object({ network = string, subnetwork = string, subnetwork_project = string }), image as object({ family = string, project = string }).
findings.title: Example's network_interface/image variables are still map(any), one hop from the module's now-strict object({...}) parameters

findings.explanation: HLD_GCP_091 ("GCE instances must not use the default VPC network") landed Unknown because network_interface.network resolves to var.network_interface["network"], a required module variable with no default — the engine can't know the value from the module alone. But the example that calls this module concretely sets network = "default" (examplea.auto.tfvars:14), which is exactly the unsafe value the policy checks for. This matters more than a bare policy violation here: the entire module is built around IAP-only reachability — no external IP, plus a custom google_compute_firewall.ssh_bastion restricted to Google's 35.235.240.0/20 IAP range. GCP's auto-created default network ships with its own pre-existing default-allow-ssh firewall rule permitting tcp:22 from 0.0.0.0/0 to every instance in that network, unless a project has explicitly deleted it — a fact this repo can't see (project/account state, not IaC). If that default rule is still present, the bastion is reachable directly from the internet on port 22 regardless of the custom firewall rule, completely bypassing the IAP-only design the rest of the module is built to enforce.
findings.remediation: Point the example at a purpose-built VPC/subnetwork instead of "default" — either reference an existing corporate network by name, or add google_compute_network/google_compute_subnetwork resources to the example and wire their names into network_interface. No custom VPC resource exists anywhere in this repo today (confirmed via grep), so this isn't a one-line value swap.
findings.title: Example resolves the bastion onto GCP's default VPC network, undermining the module's IAP-only design
